stages.name: Rulebook Lookup
stages.out: A packet: the ordered checklist of candidate factors to test (meal, sleep, medication, activity, ...) with the window to look in

selected.text: exertion in the preceding hour vs rest
days after short sleep vs normal
heart rate after meals vs between meals

rulebook_table.when: a meal was logged within 180 minutes before the item opened
rulebook_table.why_budget: 9 candidates exist; all primary plus up to 5 secondary and 2 tertiary keeps the finding readable. Strong data for most streams.

candidates.check: this meal's response vs her earlier meals of the same kind
candidates.outcome: peak glucose within 150 min of the meal
candidates.note: Food and carbohydrate load are the first-listed causes of highs.

candidates.check: evenings after a missed dose vs evenings with all doses taken
days after short sleep vs normal sleep
candidates.note: Poor or short sleep is listed as a cause of highs.
Stress hormones raise glucose.

candidates.check: days with a symptom entry vs none
candidates.note: Illness or infection is a leading listed cause.

candidates.check: meals at or after her usual latest hour vs earlier meals
candidates.note: Plausible (evening glucose tolerance is lower) but not sourced in this pass.

candidates.applies_if: patient has such a medicine listed
candidates.check: presence of steroids or similar glucose-raising medicines

candidates.her_data: verify: not confirmed to be in the store
candidates.note: Evidence is mainly type 1 diabetes; effect varies between people.

candidates.check: days with an alcohol entry vs none
candidates.note: Effect direction on glucose is mixed.

rulebook_table.when: no meal logged within 180 minutes (between meals, overnight, fasting)
rulebook_table.why_budget: 9 candidates; medication and illness lead because no meal explains it. Fewer streams are informative without a meal.

candidates.check: days with a missed dose vs none
candidates.note: Skipped doses are a first-listed cause.

candidates.check: days with a symptom entry vs none
candidates.note: Illness raises glucose through stress hormones.

candidates.check: days after short sleep vs normal
heavy or late previous dinner vs usual dinners
candidates.note: Carbohydrate load is a listed cause; carry-over to the next window is reasoned.

candidates.applies_if: only for items opening between 04:00 and 09:00
candidates.check: early-morning rise on most mornings vs this morning only
candidates.note: A repeating pattern is not a one-off event.

candidates.applies_if: patient has such a medicine listed

candidates.her_data: verify: not confirmed to be in the store

rulebook_table.when: adverse only: clinical status low, or position far
rulebook_table.why_budget: In a patient on metformin alone a true low is uncommon, so the first check is a sensor artifact. Few candidates; small budget.

candidates.check: a sudden steep drop from steady values, short run, rebound on the next reading, no meal or activity before it
candidates.outcome: shape of the reading vs its neighbours
candidates.note: Compression lows (often overnight) and new-sensor effects can read falsely low. Also check whether the low is an isolated reading.

candidates.check: gap since last meal vs her usual gap
candidates.note: Missed or delayed meals are a leading cause in people on glucose-lowering medicine.

candidates.check: activity above her usual vs normal

candidates.note: Alcohol suppresses liver glucose production.

candidates.applies_if: patient takes insulin or a sulfonylurea
candidates.check: whether insulin or a sulfonylurea is taken; dose timing vs the low
candidates.note: Metformin alone does not cause significant hypoglycemia (S5, S6).

candidates.check: illness with reduced eating vs none
candidates.note: Reasoned; not sourced in this pass.

rulebook_table.why_budget: Largest group by count and many plausible causes, so a larger budget; hourly steps are missing for this patient, which limits the activity check.

candidates.check: exertion in the preceding hour vs rest
candidates.her_data: partial (daily steps only; hourly steps not in the store)
candidates.note: Exertion is the most common physiological cause; without hourly data the test cannot isolate the hour.
Stress and anxiety release hormones that raise heart rate.
Fever and infection raise heart rate.
Dehydration raises heart rate.
Skipped for this patient: no stream.

candidates.check: days after short sleep vs normal

candidates.applies_if: patient has a thyroid condition or takes thyroid medicine
candidates.her_data: partial (condition known; TSH not in the store)

candidates.check: heart rate after meals vs between meals
candidates.note: Reasoned; small effect; not sourced in this pass.

rulebook_table.why_budget: Daily value, so tests run on days, not readings; sample sizes are small, so the budget is kept modest.

candidates.check: days after short sleep vs normal
candidates.note: Lack of sleep raises stress hormones and heart rate.

candidates.applies_if: patient has a thyroid condition or takes thyroid medicine

candidates.check: very high or very low activity vs usual
candidates.note: Reasoned; not sourced in this pass.

rulebook_table.when: last night's sleep below her usual
rulebook_table.why_budget: One strong primary cause (stress); several behavioural secondary causes with weaker data.

candidates.note: Stress is the most commonly cited cause of short-term sleep difficulty.

candidates.check: late dinner vs usual dinner time
candidates.note: Eating late is a listed cause.

candidates.her_data: partial (alcohol via diary only; no caffeine stream)

candidates.note: Screen use before bed is a listed habit; a daily total is a weak proxy.
Short-term illness disrupts sleep, but this was found only in a low-quality source.

candidates.check: travel or unusual location vs usual
candidates.note: Changing time zones disturbs sleep (S13); weather and noise are reasoned.
Uncontrolled diabetes increases urination (S18); the link to short sleep is reasoned.

rulebook_table.when: missed doses worse than her usual
rulebook_table.why_budget: Behavioural; WHO framework gives categories rather than ranked causes, so evidence is general and the budget small.

candidates.check: days with travel, events or an unusual location vs ordinary days
candidates.note: Disrupted routine and forgetfulness are patient-related adherence factors.
Psychosocial stress and depression are named in the WHO framework.
Condition-related factors (symptoms) are in the WHO framework.

candidates.check: misses in the prior days vs a clean prior week
candidates.note: Adherence barriers change over time and persist.
Reasoned; not sourced in this pass.

candidates.check: which medicine or time of day is missed most
candidates.note: Therapy-related factors (number of medicines, dose times, side effects).

rulebook_table.when: systolic or diastolic above her usual
rulebook_table.why_budget: Only a few readings a month, so tests have very few days; keep to well-sourced candidates and report small samples plainly.

candidates.applies_if: patient takes a blood pressure medicine
candidates.check: readings after a missed antihypertensive dose vs after taken doses
candidates.note: Missing blood pressure medication is commonly listed; a lower-quality source for this exact point.

candidates.check: readings at a clinic or at unusual times vs at home
candidates.note: Clinic anxiety, a full bladder and recent caffeine change readings.
Poor sleep raises blood pressure.

candidates.check: salty or festive meals vs usual meals
candidates.note: One high-salt meal can raise pressure temporarily.

candidates.check: pain or symptom days vs none

candidates.applies_if: patient has such a medicine listed

rulebook_table.when: daily fluid intake below her usual
rulebook_table.why_budget: Evidence describes causes of dehydration, not of low logged intake; budget kept small and basis marked as partly reasoned.

candidates.note: Fever, vomiting and diarrhea cause fluid loss; appetite and intake also fall when ill.

candidates.check: workload or travel days vs ordinary days
candidates.note: Forgetfulness is a reasoned cause of low intake.
Uncontrolled diabetes increases urination and dehydration risk.

candidates.check: hot or humid days vs ordinary days
candidates.note: Heat increases fluid need.

rulebook_table.when: daily screen time above her usual
rulebook_table.why_budget: No clinical evidence base. Recorded but not used to generate findings until a doctor-advisor decides otherwise.

candidates.check: deadline or workload days vs ordinary days
candidates.note: No clinical evidence; behavioural proxy.
No clinical evidence; behavioural proxy.
